label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8), keyed to first original token
explanation: Almost entirely a delimiter-step feature: 97% of activation mass is at the <DEL> input (t == L), where the model is about to output the first original token. It is gated by length: it essentially never fires for L <= 6, rarely for L = 7 (2% of mass), and most strongly for L = 9 (63% of mass, 38% of L=9 delimiters active). Within long sequences, whether it fires and how strongly depends on the first original token (the token to be output next): h, x, 1, m have the highest rates (about 3x lift) and contribute the top activations (all top-12 examples begin with h or x), followed by 0, r, f, z, o, 3, l, i. It does not fire in the copy phase at all; a small residue (~3% of mass) fires weakly on the last one or two original tokens of L=8/9 sequences, just before <DEL>. Delimiter + L>=8 alone gives recall 0.91 but precision 0.31; adding the first-token set raises F1 to about 0.60, but the first-token dependence is graded instead of a clean set, so precision and recall stay incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: h, x, 1, m, 0, r; least: k, v, t, w) and the previous input (most: e, f, d, s, x, 0; least: g, o, 2, p); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=8, L=9 & t=9.
